foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption persists over the next 30 days, with 68% pressure and 78% state confirmation feeding through energy supply shock, keeping the forecast near 67%.
foil.perspective_strategic: The Red Sea disruption state, with 68% pressure and 78% state confirmation, signals a stable energy repricing risk, with the strongest transmission path running through energy supply shock toward Energy, per the canonical state path.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level and the absence of new hard signals suggest that energy repricing risk could stall if large importers and policy officials successfully stabilize supply chains, preventing a break above the current baseline.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 67%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 68% pressure and 78% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
